title: Needle-in-Haystack Telemetry Scorer for Cross-Tenant Usage/Cost/Latency Signals
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: Our current alert pipeline flags many noisy events across usage, cost, and latency streams that either affect only single long-tail tenants or are explainable by benign operational changes. This ticket implements a cross-tenant, context-aware scoring service (the 'Needle-in-Haystack Scorer') that raises only high-value signals and attaches concise attribution to reduce pager fatigue and improve incident TTR.

Scope: Build a scoring microservice and enrichment layer that consumes existing aggregated telemetry (minute-resolution usage/cost/latency), supplements with lightweight traces and configuration context (model variant, plan tier, routing policy), and produces a ranked list of actionable candidate alerts with an explainability blob (top contributing features and probable root cause). The service will feed the existing alert orchestration system and the Console UI.

Non-goals: This ticket does not replace the core threshold rules or the long-running ML drift detectors; instead it provides a secondary scoring tier and rationale to prioritize and suppress alerts. It also does not include extensive per-tenant ML training — we will use hybrid heuristics plus simple statistical/causal signals initially.
acceptance_criteria: Service ingests minute-level usage/cost/latency rollups from telemetry-kafka topic and enriches events with model variant and tenant plan from config-store
Generates a per-candidate score (0-100) and top-3 contributing factors for 95% of candidates within 250ms of ingestion in staging
Default policy reduces noisy notifications (historical false-positive > 80%) by at least 40% for a selected pilot of 50 tenants
Explainability blob includes: signal delta, cohort baseline, correlated dimension (e.g., region or model-variant), and recent rollout flag if applicable
End-to-end tests cover data-loss, backfill correctness, and graceful degradation when enrichment sources are unavailable
Console shows scored candidates with sort/filter by score, tenant, signal type, and a link to the attribution details
design_notes:
High level design: 1) Ingest: kafka consumer in console-telemetry-cluster reads aggregated rollups. 2) Enrichment: join by tenant_id to config-store API (cache with TTL) & tracing-lite service for recent request spike signatures. 3) Scoring: compute ensemble score = weighted sum of anomaly-zscore, sudden-cohort-shift, tenant-exposure-adjuster, and rollout-penalty. Tunable weights via feature flags. 4) Explainability: return top contributors using simple SHAP-like attribution for ensemble inputs. 5) Output: publish scored candidates to telemetry-alerts-scored topic and persist top-k per-tenant in Postgres for UI.

Implementation choices: start with deterministic heuristic models (robust z-scores, EWMA drift, cohort ratio) to keep results interpretable. Add a light LGBM classifier later for edge cases if pilot shows need. Caching config-store responses and using in-memory prefix aggregation will keep latency within bounds.

Privacy/Cost trade-offs: minimize retention of raw traces; only include sketch/signature hashes and metadata. Keep enrichment calls rate-limited to avoid blowing up cost when alerts surge.
implementation_tasks: Create scoring microservice scaffold (Go) with kafka consumer/producer clients
Implement enrichment cache layer for config-store and model-variant map
Implement base heuristics: robust z-score, EWMA shift, cohort-ratio with exposure normalization
Implement explainability generator that emits top-3 contributors and textual summary
Add feature flags and remote-config knobs for weight tuning
Publish outputs to telemetry-alerts-scored and write persistence for top-k per-tenant
Add unit/integration tests and write e2e pipeline validation job
Add metrics: processing latency histogram, scoring distribution, suppression rate, false-positive estimate
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): deploy scorer to staging cluster with kafka topic mirror, run in shadow-mode for 2 weeks to collect scoring distribution. Phase 2 (pilot): enable scoring for 50 low-risk tenants; route high-score candidates to Console but keep notifications off; gather feedback and false-positive labels. Phase 3 (opt-in): allow tenants to opt-in to scored notifications with default suppression policy. Phase 4 (wider rollout): gate by telemetry budget and observed improvement in signal precision. Emergency kill-switch and topic-disable feature flags available.
metrics_and_observability: Expose Prometheus metrics: scorer_latency_ms, candidates_consumed_total, candidates_emitted_total, suppression_rate, avg_score_by_signal_type. Add Grafana dashboard with score histogram, top contributing dimensions, pilot tenant precision/recall estimates. Emit structured audit events to logging pipeline for every emitted candidate to support RCA.
risks_and_mitigations: Incorrect suppression of real incidents: default conservative threshold; pilot mode keeps notifications off until manual review
Enrichment unavailability causes score degradation: fallback to baseline heuristics and mark explainability as partial
Cost blow-up if enrichment calls scale: cache, rate-limit, and batch enrichment queries
Data skew between staging and prod: use mirrored topics and synthetic traffic to validate distributions
testing_notes: Create synthetic workloads that simulate: tenant-specific cost spikes, global model rollout causing latency increases for a model-variant cohort, and benign traffic pattern changes (e.g., scheduled backup windows). Validate suppression reduction and ensure explainability maps to injected root causes. Include chaos test where config-store returns 500 to verify fallback path.
security_considerations: Do not store PII in the explainability blob. Use tenant_id hashed at rest. Service must authenticate to config-store via mTLS. Follow existing KMS patterns for any stored secrets. Ensure logs redact API keys and request bodies.
notes_and_links: Related tickets: ENG-168442 (rollout tagging), ENG-174210 (config-store caching), ENG-172001 (telemetry reliability epic)
